sections.description: Overview of the child's presenting history, physical findings, and the first-line ICU stabilization and drainage procedures that set the stage for further investigations.
subtopics: History of presenting illness: timeline of chest pain, dyspnoea, and respiratory distress
Physical examination findings: respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, chest percussion and auscultation, abdominal assessment
Initial ICU stabilization: humidified oxygen, monitoring, and laboratory ordering
Basic imaging: chest X‑ray and bedside lung ultrasound findings of right pleural effusion
Early therapeutic thoracocentesis: volume and appearance of aspirated fluid, immediate clinical response

sections.description: Systematic assessment of laboratory and imaging data that guides the identification of a pancreatopleural fistula while excluding other causes of haemorrhagic pleural effusion.
subtopics: Pleural fluid analysis – macroscopic appearance, protein, LDH, cell counts, cytology, and ADA
Serum and pleural fluid amylase/lipase concentrations and their diagnostic significance
Imaging modalities – contrast‑enhanced CT chest and MRCP – sensitivity, specificity, and typical findings
Differential diagnoses considered: tuberculosis, empyema, malignancy, oesophageal perforation, diaphragmatic hernia, hepatic hydrothorax
Diagnostic reasoning: integration of trauma history, fluid characteristics, enzyme elevation and imaging to confirm PPF

sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Etiology of Pancreatopleural Fistula
sections.description: Anatomical, physiological and etiologic mechanisms that enable pancreatic fluid leakage into the pleural cavity, with emphasis on pediatric-specific triggers.
subtopics: Anatomical route of pancreatic fluid: posterior duct rupture, retroperitoneal spread, diaphragmatic hiatus entry, pleural contact
Triggers of ductal disruption: blunt abdominal trauma, acute pancreatitis, chronic pancreatitis
Genetic predispositions in children: PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR, and their impact on pancreatic duct integrity
Clinical presentation versus underlying abdominal pathology – the ‘pulmonary mask’ phenomenon
Relation between pleural fluid amylase isoenzyme (pancreatic vs salivary) and differential diagnosis

sections.description: Evidence‑based, stepwise therapeutic strategies for PPF, highlighting conservative care, endoscopic interventions, and surgical options in the pediatric population.
subtopics: Conservative management: nil per‑oral diet, total parenteral nutrition, octreotide dosing (30 µg/kg/day), pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy, chest‑tube drainage monitoring
Endoscopic therapy: ERCP indications, surgical sphincterotomy, trans‑papillary ductal stenting, expected success rates
Surgical options: distal pancreatectomy, pancreaticojejunostomy, cystojejunostomy – indications, procedural overview, pediatric outcomes
Monitoring and criteria for fistula closure: drainage volume trends, repeat imaging, laboratory normalization
Tailoring therapy in the absence of formal guidelines: individualized decision making based on clinical response

sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s recovery trajectory, long‑term outcomes, and the broader lessons for clinicians regarding early recognition, appropriate therapy, and avoidance of misdiagnosis.
subtopics: Clinical course after initiating octreotide and TPN: drainage reduction, chest‑tube removal timeline
Discharge details and post‑hospital monitoring schedule
Long‑term follow‑up: symptom resolution, lifestyle adjustments, return to school activities
Prognosis and recurrence rates in pediatric PPF
Key clinical insights: importance of trauma history, pleural fluid amylase testing, MRCP utility, and preventing unnecessary anti‑TB treatment
